Class BehaviorBindingTable

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.BehaviorBindingTable
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.AuthoritativeDeclarations, com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.ServerTierBridge
public final class BehaviorBindingTable extends Object implements com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.ServerTierBridge, com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.AuthoritativeDeclarations
MKC's server-authoritative behavior store — the implementation of MK's two server-tier ports (ServerTierBridge write side, AuthoritativeDeclarations read/AXIS-1 side). Registered with ServerTier.install(...) at MKC init so the engine routes server-tier declarations here and consults this above the client cascade.

Authority + the presence fast-path

This holds the SERVER-tier declarations (gating, drop-rule, …) keyed by Address, with the same per-slot > per-group walk the client engine uses, but at server authority. resolve(Address, BehaviorKey) returns the server's winning Decl.Set, or Decl.inherit() when the server does not override (so the engine falls through to the client tier / library default).

isEmpty() / hasBinding(Address) back the "the slots nobody touches stay exactly vanilla" guarantee: the Phase-4 server seam early-outs on any address with no binding, so an un-addressed slot incurs zero library logic.

(The store/walk mirrors the MK client engine's — the cascade algorithm is the same; the two tiers differ only in authority and side, not in shape.)
